classification.difficultyReason: Relate a cubic divisor to a quadratic factor and recover a new remainder from an unknown polynomial.

content.prompt: When $P(x)$ is divided by $x^3+2x^2-5x-6$, the remainder is $3x^2+2x+1$. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2+4x+3$.

answer.short:
$-10x-8$.

Factor the divisors and evaluate at $x=-1$ and $x=-3$ to determine the linear remainder.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^3+2x^2-5x-6&=(x-2)(x+1)(x+3)\\x^2+4x+3&=(x+1)(x+3).\end{align*}$$
The supplied division identity gives
$$P(x)=(x-2)(x+1)(x+3)Q(x)+3x^2+2x+1.$$
Thus,
$$\begin{align*}P(-1)&=3(-1)^2+2(-1)+1\\P(-1)&=2\\P(-3)&=3(-3)^2+2(-3)+1\\P(-3)&=22.\end{align*}$$
Write the remainder on division by $(x+1)(x+3)$ as $R(x)=Ax+B$. Substitution gives
$$\begin{align*}-A+B&=2\\-3A+B&=22.\end{align*}$$
Solving simultaneously gives $A=-10$ and $B=-8$. Hence, the remainder is $-10x-8$.
